market_holds: Sealed baseline (2026-11-09 18:10 UTC): spot 11.50, front-expiry (11-13) straddle 12.3%, event-implied move 8.27%, 25d skew +7.6 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.52, 20d realised vol 107%. Run-up: -16% over 20 days but +14% over 5 days; the stock went 10.38 (11-04) -> 9.05 (11-05, sector selloff, no company news) -> 10.68 (11-06) -> ~11.52 (11-09 intraday), i.e. +27% in two sessions as IonQ beat and raised (Nov 5 amc) and the whole quantum basket (RGTI, IONQ, QUBT) moved together. Down ~45% since the Aug 6 print and 64% off the 52w high. Consensus Q3 revenue $4.0-4.4M (Earnings Whispers ~$4.0M, Benzinga $4.3M, Chartmill $4.42M, EPS -$0.10; whisper -$0.16, more pessimistic), with the next-quarter revenue estimate cut ~69% over 3 months (Chartmill) after both 2026 system deliveries were pushed to Q4 on the Q2 call; FY26 consensus ~$42.5M implies ~$36.5M in H2. No formal quarterly guide. Revenue has missed three quarters running. Last four reactions -9.3%, -7.0%, +2.5%, -8.5%; the line it trades on is the Q4 system-delivery timing (FAU $20M Advantage2 plus a second system), bookings after a front-loaded H1 ($35.5M, Q2 only $2.1M), and RPO ($40.7M).
view: This is a sector-beta name walking into a print with a known shape: Q3 carries no system revenue, so the headline is QCaaS plus services against a ~$4M bar that sits ~30% above Q2's $3.08M, and a fourth straight revenue miss is more likely than not. But the estimate has already been cut hard and the stock is down 45% since August, so a small miss alone is close to priced. The release will be judged on two things the price has not settled either way: whether management reaffirms both Q4 system deliveries (FAU's own and third-party items through October still describe the Advantage2 install as 'later this year' with no commissioning news; nothing found says it slipped), and what Q3 bookings look like after a front-loaded H1 with no system-sale announcement since August (only an LG CNS non-binding MOU, a Shionogi research prize and a solver update in the 8-Ks of Oct 28 and Nov 4). The most likely release is a reaffirmed Q4, soft Q3 revenue and thin Q3 bookings. That historically sells off (three of the last four prints fell 7-9%), and this time the stock has just bounced 27% in two sessions on a peer's beat rather than on its own news, which leaves room to give some back. Against that: sentiment is washed out, the whisper is below consensus, and a clean reaffirmation, or a booking bundled with the release as D-Wave sometimes does, could squeeze a heavily sold, high-beta name higher. Rigetti reports after the close on Nov 10, outside the window. Net: a mild lean down that I would not bet on.

recommendation.reason: The pattern (revenue miss, thin bookings, sell-off) and the fresh 27% sector-driven bounce lean down, but consensus has been cut ~69%, the whisper is already below it, and the options skew already pays for downside. The deciding item is a binary on Q4 delivery and booking commentary that I found no dated public trace of in either direction, so I cannot show the price is behind.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An explicit reaffirmation that the FAU system and the second system ship/recognise in Q4 with FY revenue held near ~$40M, or a new system booking announced with the release, would likely send the stock up; a slip of either system into 2027 would make it a large down move.

self_critique: The stock is down 45% since the last print, the whisper and sentiment are already bearish, and the skew already pays for downside, so a 'soft but on track' print may be a relief rally in a heavily sold, high-beta name. The sector tape after IonQ is supportive, and D-Wave has a habit of pairing results with upbeat commercial announcements. My lean rests mostly on the base rate of the last four prints and the shape of the run-in, not on a dated fact the price lacks.
approach_notes: P4 (priced in is a claim to prove) helped. The Chartmill revision and the whisper showed that the Q3 revenue miss is mostly priced, so I did not lean on it. P3's physical/customer route (FAU install status) was the right question but has no public trace before the release. The playbook gives no guidance for sector-beta names whose run-in is driven by a peer.
